blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) on Tuesday, Nov. 17, warned that individuals who assaulted police officers during a rally may face criminal charges after several personnel were injured in the incident. “Let this be clear: We will not allow violence against our police officers to go unanswered,” NCRPO chief Brig. Gen. Christopher Abrahano said in a statement. READ: Protesters, police clash in Manila during Asean Summit protest The November 15 altercations at Liwasang Bonifacio resulted in the injury of 15 personnel and the arrest of eight individuals after confrontations between rallyists and police escalated.
